main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem} For every $1/2<\gamma<3/2$ and every nonnegative $W\in L^{\gamma+1/2}(\R)$, $\Tr(H_{-W})_-^\gamma \le 2\left(\frac{\gamma-1/2}{\gamma+1/2}\right)^{\gamma-1/2} L_{\gamma,1}^{\cl}\int_\R W^{\gamma+1/2}$. The constant is optimal and equals $L_{\gamma,1}^{(1)}$. More precisely, if $r=(\gamma-1/2)^{-1}$, equality is attained by $W(x)=(r+1)\sech^2(rx)$. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: The one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring conjecture holds on the whole open interval 1/2<γ<3/2: summing all negative eigenvalue moments of −d²/dx²−W never beats the constant obtained from a single bound state (Keller's sech² optimizer). Sibling manuscripts: the same constant for finite-matrix potentials of any size (M), and all equality cases are direct sums of independently scaled/centred scalar sech² solitons in one constant basis (E).

main_statement.match_check: Exact for 262-S Theorem 1.1 (bound, optimality, identification with the one-state constant, attainment at (r+1)sech²(rx)). The comparator's moment is a supremum over finite orthonormal families of weak eigenfunctions of the H¹ form rather than the operator's spectral sum; the sibling theorem OperatorProof.sharp_lieb_thirring_spectral (SpectralMain.lean, after Main) constructs the self-adjoint form operator unconditionally and proves spectralMoment = negativeMoment, closing that gap. Bochner-integral junk values are not an issue: for admissible W and v∈H¹, W|v|² is integrable (W∈L^p, |v|²∈L¹∩L^∞). Comparator challenge text equals Model.lean definitions (textual check of the 15 signature-closure defs). Signed-potential Corollary 7.3 is not formalized.
main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: 262-S Thm 1.1 completely (plus sibling operator-formulation theorem). Not formalized: Cor 7.3 (signed potentials); the whole of 262-M (finite-matrix inequality, integrated trace comparison Thm 3.1) and 262-E (equality classification). The paper's Thm 2.1 action inequality appears in Lean only as an unused Prop `ActionClaim` (MatrixOrder.lean:84, never proved as stated); the route proves the equivalent-for-purpose `finite_action_upper_test` (IntervalAction.lean:154) for continuous amplitudes with classical derivatives.

proof_architecture.claim: Reduce to a potential-free finite-interval action inequality with individual scales: sup_{C lower tri} E_K(Cu) ≥ Σ∫(k_i²−s²)^σ (Thm 2.1).
Build the regularized field M_δ (s-integrated functional calculus of K²−2sB+s²), show it is a trace gradient with C¹ primitive J, compute μ, directional Jensen bound, diagonal rule and J(−K)−J(K).
Rank-one comparison: M(B)=aaᵀ ⇒ aᵀ(K²−B²)a ≥ |a|^{2q}, via resolvent tangent inequality at Y_s=(sI−B)²+dI, Gaussian-mixture conjugation average, and Klein's inequality.
Existence of lower-triangular C and path B with εB'=M(B)−aaᵀ, B: K→−K, by mod-2 continuation modulo row signs and barrier confinement.
Action identity (J(B)+aᵀBa)'=2a'ᵀBa−ε^{-1}‖M−aaᵀ‖² + completed square + compact penalty limit ε→0, then δ→0.
Spectral passage: ordered eigenfunctions + triangularity + Young duality give Σk_j^{2γ} ≤ ℓ_σ∫W^p on intervals; exhaust the line by cutoffs/min–max; sharpness by sech².

(262-M) Replace step 3 by the integrated trace comparison tr(NV) ≥ tr(N^q) with exact deficit (half-line Riccati boundary maps, log-det integral, HS square) to allow densities of any rank; realify complex W.

(262-E) Retain defects with dimension-free constant; compactness with m columns gives pointwise algebraic relations at equality; constant channels and matrix Riccati B_0'=r(B_0²−α²) give tanh/sech² profiles; attainment by factorization.

eureka_candidates.for: Syntactically tiny (one integral of a scalar function of an affine matrix pencil), occurs nowhere in the goal, and the whole proof is about it: it is simultaneously a trace gradient (so the path ODE has a primitive), equals (K²−B²)^σ on commuting data (so the endpoint integral is the spectral sum), and satisfies the rank-one Young comparison. The paper presents it as designed from the identity k²−2sb+s²=(s−b)²+k²−b². Closes a ~50-year-old conjecture on the full open interval. Lean-formalized and load-bearing (~69% of the mathematical core).

The rank-one comparison's tools are textbook. The field is specific to this inequality; reuse beyond LT-type problems is unclear (one-off device risk).
